title: Scoring Shaft's Big Score with Gordon Parks and Tom McIntosh
summary: He wrote five or six cues for the film, including Joe Williams's song, working with Tom McIntosh, Dick Hazard and Gordon Parks.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: How about the tunes that were on the Tonight Show last night? Which ones were they that you --
Oh. This was -- one of the tunes was interestingly enough was in 'Shaft's Second Score.' With Gordon Parks.
Well, I wrote about five arrangements, five or six cues in the picture.
I know you did. Yeah, you worked with Tom MacIntosh on that picture, right?
Yeah. Very close. Tom and Gordon Parks and so Joe eventually wanted a score from me.
We had a great staff of musicians there. Beautiful orchestra and great arrangers. There was Dick Hazard, who did most of the conducting. We were all free to do it --

Yes, that's right. Because Tom was in the booth with Gordon at that time, you know, and discussing what this meant and what that meant and what this music meant to the picture. Because you know you have the very big screen there, and you have to explain to people the semantics, musically what it means, you know? So Dale -- who -- I think I said Dale Ehler (PHONETIC) and Dick Hazard -- there was no way for the music to miss.
Because these people are so highly qualified, and it was a great team to work with, you know?
And that's a lot of fun.
